title: The Day of Dhu Qarad • On the Road to Khaybar • The Morning at Khaybar

blocks.1: Three nights before setting out for Khaybar, a morning came on the edge of Madinah. Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA) himself told the story of that morning. The Prophet’s {{1}} milch camels were grazing in the pastures of Dhu Qarad. With them was his slave Rabah (RA). Salamah had gone that way that day with the horse of Talhah ibn ‘Ubaydillah (RA). At dawn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Fazari attacked with his band. He killed one of the herdsmen. He began driving off the herd of camels. Salamah (RA) said to Rabah, take this horse to Talhah. Tell the Prophet {{2}} that the polytheists have taken his camels. He himself stood up on a hill. Facing Madinah he cried out three times, Ya sabahah! Morning calamity, help! Then he ran alone after the raiders. He was shooting arrows and chanting,
blocks.3: I am the son of al-Akwa‘; today is the day of the ruin of the base.{{1}}
blocks.4: Whoever he caught up with, the arrow would go through the saddle and straight up to the shoulder. Whenever someone turned around, Salamah would sit down at the foot of a tree and shoot that rider’s horse. When they entered a narrow mountain pass he would climb the mountain and chase them, hurling stones. In this way not one camel of the Prophet’s {{1}} remained in their hands. In their flight they left behind more than thirty cloaks and thirty spears. Salamah put a stone over each one as a mark, so that the Companions of the Prophet {{2}} might come and recognise them. They sat down in one place to eat breakfast. Salamah sat on top of a hill. The son of Badr al-Fazari said, who is that man? They said, he has not left our tail since dawn. He has snatched away everything we had in hand. He said, four of you go and catch him. Four got up and came. As soon as they came within earshot, Salamah (RA) said, do you know me? They said, no, who are you? He said, I am Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘. By the One who honoured Muhammad {{3}}, I can catch whichever of you I wish, and none of you can catch me. One said, I think so too. They turned back. Salamah did not leave his place. A little later, through the gaps in the trees, he saw the horsemen of the Prophet {{4}} coming. First of all, Akhram al-Asadi (RA). Behind him Abu Qatadah al-Ansari (RA), and further behind, Miqdad ibn al-Aswad (RA). Salamah caught Akhram’s horse by the rein. He said, Akhram, beware of them. Wait until the Prophet {{5}} and the Companions arrive. Akhram (RA) said, Salamah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day, and know that Paradise is true and Hell is true, then do not come between me and martyrdom. Salamah let go. Akhram and ‘Abd al-Rahman fought. Akhram cut the legs of ‘Abd al-Rahman’s horse; ‘Abd al-Rahman martyred Akhram with a spear and mounted his horse. Abu Qatadah went after him and finished him with a spear thrust. Even then Salamah did not stop. He had no horse; he ran on foot. So fast that behind him not even the dust of the Companions of the Prophet {{6}} could be seen any more. Before sunset he caught up with them near the spring of Dhu Qarad. They were thirsty, going down to drink water. Salamah drove them away from there; he did not let even a drop of water touch their mouths. He pierced one of them again with an arrow and said, take this, I am the son of al-Akwa‘, today is the day of the ruin of the base. The man cried out, may his mother weep for him! Are you that al-Akwa‘ who has been after us since dawn? Salamah said, yes, enemy of your own self, that very al-Akwa‘. In the evening when he reached the Prophet {{7}}, all the camels, spears and cloaks he had snatched back were in the hands of the Prophet {{8}}. Bilal (RA) had slaughtered one of those camels and was roasting its liver and hump for the Prophet {{9}}. Salamah said, O Messenger of Allah, let me pick a hundred men. I will pursue them and finish them all. Not one will be left to give news. The Prophet {{10}} smiled so that in the firelight his molars were visible. He said, Salamah, could you really do this? Salamah said, yes, by the One who has honoured you. The Prophet {{11}} said, now they have reached Ghatafan. There they are being entertained. In the morning the Prophet {{12}} said,
blocks.6: Today our best horseman is Abu Qatadah, and our best infantryman is Salamah.{{1}}
blocks.7: Then he gave Salamah two shares, the horseman’s share and the infantryman’s share, both together. On the way back to Madinah he seated him behind himself on the back of his she-camel al-‘Adba’. No horse, no companion. Yet the one who ran alone and brought back the whole herd, the Prophet {{1}} lifted up behind himself. We often think, what can I do alone? I have no manpower, no horse. Salamah did not think any of this. Before him there was just one matter: the camels belong to the Prophet {{2}}. The work was in front of him, so he went and caught it. He did not sit waiting for the rest to arrive. On the way back an Ansari began calling out, will anyone race me to Madinah? No one? Over and over, the same words. Salamah (RA) said, do you not respect even an honourable man? The man said, no, except the Messenger of Allah. Salamah said, O Messenger of Allah, my parents be sacrificed for you, let me get down. The Prophet {{3}} said, if you wish. Salamah got down and ran. He stayed a little behind for a hill or two, then he caught up with the man and, giving a slap between the shoulders, said, I’ve got you. The man said, so it seems. Salamah reached Madinah first. He did not get down without informing the one on whose camel he was sitting behind. Permission even before entering a race. By Allah, not even three nights had passed in Madinah when we set out with the Prophet {{4}} on the road to Khaybar, Salamah used to say.{{5}}
blocks.9: About a month and a half after returning from Hudaybiyah, at the beginning of the seventh year of Hijrah, the Prophet {{1}} set out toward Khaybar. It was the biggest fortress-city of the Jews, north of Madinah; the exiles of Banu al-Nadir had sat right there and built the alliance of the Confederates at the Trench. Only those who had been at Hudaybiyah went along.{{2}}
blocks.10: Those who had sat at home with excuses on the journey of Hudaybiyah also sensed it: Khaybar was ahead. Smelling the spoils, they wanted to go along. The Qur’an had said this beforehand in this way,
blocks.12: (O Muslims!) When you go to gather spoils of war, those who stayed behind (from the journey of Hudaybiyah) will say, let us go with you as well. They want to change the word of Allah. Tell them, you shall never come with us. Allah had said so before. Then they will say, in fact you bear envy toward us. No; rather they are such people that they understand very little of speech.{{1}}
blocks.13: Those who were not to be found on the journey of hardship are the very first on the journey of profit. We know such companions. Busy on the day of work, present on the day of sharing. Allah had made the account clear that very day: whoever was not in the hardship will not be in the fruit either. A night road. One of the caravan said, ‘Amir, won’t you recite some of your little verses for us! ‘Amir ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA) was a poet. Coming down and driving the camels along he began to sing,
blocks.15: O Allah, if not for You we would not have found guidance, nor given charity, nor prayed. So forgive, we are ransomed for You; when we face the enemy keep our feet firm, and send down tranquillity upon us.{{1}}
blocks.16: The Prophet {{1}} asked, who is singing? The people said, ‘Amir. He said, may Allah have mercy on him. In the battle of Khaybar ‘Amir (RA) went to strike a Jew with his sword; the sword was short, it came back and hit his own knee. He was martyred from that very wound. People began to say, ‘Amir’s deeds have been wasted, he killed himself. On the way back the Prophet {{2}} took the hand of his nephew Salamah (RA) and asked, what is the matter? Salamah said, my parents be sacrificed for you, people are saying ‘Amir’s deeds have been wasted. The Prophet {{3}} said,
blocks.18: Whoever said this has said wrongly. For him there are two rewards; he was a hard worker, a mujahid in the way of Allah.{{1}}
blocks.19: What appeared from the outside was an accident. What was written with Allah was two rewards. The Prophet {{1}} did not pass judgement on the outcome of others’ deeds as easily as we do. Reaching the mouth of a valley on the way, the Companions, in joy, raised their voices in takbir: Allahu akbar! Allahu akbar! La ilaha illa Allah! The Prophet {{2}} said,
blocks.21: Be gentle with yourselves. You are not calling a deaf one, nor an absent one. You are calling One who is All-Hearing, very near, and He is with you.{{1}}
blocks.23: Moving toward a fortress-city. Voices heavy, chests swelling. Even at this moment the Prophet {{1}} reminded them that the One being called is not far away. There is no need to shout to make Him hear. We often make du‘a by raising a cry, as if Allah were somewhere far. Yet He is right with us. Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA) was then behind the Prophet’s {{2}} mount. He was saying to himself, la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. The Prophet {{3}} heard and called, ‘Abdullah ibn Qays! Abu Musa said, at your service, O Messenger of Allah. The Prophet {{4}} said, shall I tell you a phrase from the treasure of Paradise? Abu Musa said, certainly, O Messenger of Allah, my parents be sacrificed for you. The Prophet {{5}} said,
blocks.25: La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah. This is one of the treasures of Paradise.{{1}}
blocks.26: The Companions were going on a journey of victory. And one of them was saying to himself the very phrase whose meaning is: I have no power, I have no strength, everything is Allah’s. The Prophet {{1}} called exactly that a treasure of Paradise. The nearer victory comes, the more tempting the thought of one’s own strength becomes. That phrase there is a rein.
blocks.28: He halted at a place called Sahba, very near Khaybar. After praying ‘Asr he asked for food. For the whole army only barley meal was found. Everyone mixed it in water and chewed it. The Prophet {{1}} rinsed his mouth, and so did the Companions. Then they prayed Maghrib.{{2}}
blocks.29: Those who were going toward a fortress-city had barley meal as their provisions. When we set out on a journey we lengthen the list of food. Their list was short, their goal big. At night they reached near Khaybar. On reaching a settlement by night, the Prophet {{1}} would not attack before morning. He would wait, keep listening; on hearing the adhan he would halt, and only if he did not hear it would he attack.{{2}}
blocks.30: In the morning the people of Khaybar came out to the fields with spades and baskets. Seeing the army in front of them they shouted, Muhammad! By Allah, Muhammad and his army! The Prophet {{1}} said,
blocks.32: Allahu akbar, Khaybar is ruined. When we descend on the courtyard of a people, evil is the morning of those who were warned.{{1}}
blocks.33: Even on the night of war, a wait for an adhan. Where Allah’s name was uttered, the sword did not descend. Not striking merely because one has the power; first being sure on whom one is striking. Fortress after fortress fell. The fortress for which the banner of victory was placed in the hand of ‘Ali (RA), that story has been told before, in Dars 4. At Khaybar sixteen Muslims were martyred. Ninety-three Jews were killed.{{1}}
blocks.34: Fortress after fortress came into their hands. Fields, gardens, date groves. Those who had spent year after year in Madinah’s houses on dates and water; ‘A’ishah (RA) has told their words: when Khaybar was conquered we said, now we will eat dates to our fill.{{1}}
blocks.35: The nation that once thought eating dates to its fill was the fruit of victory, Allah then laid before it the keys of great empires. This promise the Qur’an had already announced, in two steps,
blocks.37: Allah has promised you abundant spoils, which you will seize. He has granted you this victory immediately and withheld the hands of people from you, so that it may be a sign for the believers and that He may guide you to the straight path. There is yet another victory, which has not so far come within your power, but Allah has kept it within His own grasp. Allah is fully able over all things.{{1}}
blocks.38: The immediate victory is Khaybar; and another victory, still beyond reach of power, but encircled by Allah’s hand. What is out of my reach today may fall into my hand tomorrow from inside Allah’s encirclement. We see only today’s account.

footnotes.0: Sahih Muslim 1807; Sahih al-Bukhari 4194 (a rhythmic rajaz). ‘Rudda‘’ is a plural; the rendering in the sense of ‘lowly’ or ‘cowardly’ is a free translation.
footnotes.1: Sahih Muslim 1807; Sunan Abi Dawud 2752 (al-Albani: hasan sahih). The Prophet {{1}} gave him the horseman’s share and the infantryman’s share, both together; later he seated him behind himself on the she-camel named al-‘Adba’.
footnotes.2: Sahih Muslim 1807 (Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA)’s own narration, via his son Iyas; sahih); its abridged form is Sahih al-Bukhari 4194; Sunan Abi Dawud 2752 (al-Albani: hasan sahih). ‘Ya sabahah’ is a cry of calamity. The ‘translation’ of ‘al-yawm yawm al-rudda‘’ is a free rendering. Timing: Salamah himself said, before three nights had passed we set out for Khaybar; the dars keeps this order of Muslim. In some Sirah books the time of Dhu Qarad is placed earlier; there is disagreement about the timing. The camels were the Prophet’s {{1}} milch herd (liqah).
footnotes.3: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Fath 48:15, note 11, p. 371 (Allah had directed the Prophet {{1}} that in the Khaybar expedition only the participants of Hudaybiyah would go). Time frame: returning from Hudaybiyah, staying in Madinah for the rest of Dhu al-Hijjah and part of Muharram, setting out in Muharram of 7 AH (Ibn Ishaq ← Ibn Hisham); ‘about a month and a half’ is a calculation.
footnotes.4: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Fath 48:15, pp. 370–371 (matched word for word by reading the printed page); notes 10–12: for those who showed sacrifice and endurance on the journey of Hudaybiyah, as a reward Allah had promised another victory before the conquest of Makkah; the hint is toward Khaybar. The hypocrites who stayed behind at Hudaybiyah will want to go along out of greed for spoils; Allah’s command was that only the participants of Hudaybiyah would go on the Khaybar expedition. (Note 12: this command is not in any separate verse of the Qur’an; it was given to the Prophet {{1}} through revelation.)
footnotes.5: Sahih al-Bukhari 4196 (from Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA)). A portion of the poem.
footnotes.6: Sahih al-Bukhari 4196, 6891 (from Salamah ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA)). ‘Amir ibn al-Akwa‘ (RA) was Salamah’s uncle (in Sahih Muslim 1807, ‘my uncle ‘Amir’). The account of the short sword striking his own knee is in this very hadith.
footnotes.7: Sahih al-Bukhari 4205 (Khaybar chapter; also in Sahih Muslim 2704), 6610 (from Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA)): ‘When the Prophet {{1}} set out for Khaybar, the people climbed above a valley and cried out loudly Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah. The Prophet {{2}} said: be gentle with yourselves; you are not calling a deaf one, nor an absent one; you are calling One who is All-Hearing, very near, and He is with you.’ Abu Musa (RA) was then behind the Prophet’s {{3}} mount; hearing his ‘la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah’ the Prophet {{4}} called to him and said, ‘the phrase of one of the treasures of Paradise’ (Bukhari 4205: agreed upon). Sahih al-Jami‘ 7864 (al-Albani: sahih). Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 621 places the same event on the return from Khaybar; in the Bukhari text it is at the time of setting out for Khaybar, and the dars follows that text.
footnotes.8: Sahih al-Bukhari 4205 (Khaybar chapter; also in Sahih Muslim 2704), 6610 (from Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA)): ‘When the Prophet {{1}} set out for Khaybar, the people climbed above a valley and cried out loudly Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah. The Prophet {{2}} said: be gentle with yourselves; you are not calling a deaf one, nor an absent one; you are calling One who is All-Hearing, very near, and He is with you.’ Abu Musa (RA) was then behind the Prophet’s {{3}} mount; hearing his ‘la hawla wa la quwwata illa billah’ the Prophet {{4}} called to him and said, ‘the phrase of one of the treasures of Paradise’ (Bukhari 4205: agreed upon). Sahih al-Jami‘ 7864 (al-Albani: sahih). Al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 621 places the same event on the return from Khaybar; in the Bukhari text it is at the time of setting out for Khaybar, and the dars follows that text.
footnotes.9: Sahih al-Bukhari 4205 (agreed upon; from Abu Musa al-Ash‘ari (RA): a phrase from the treasure of Paradise).
footnotes.10: Sahih al-Bukhari 215, 4195 (from Suwayd ibn al-Nu‘man (RA)): ‘We went out with the Prophet {{1}} in the year of Khaybar; reaching Sahba he prayed ‘Asr, then asked for food, and nothing could be brought except barley meal (sawiq). We chewed it and ate. Then he asked for water and rinsed his mouth, and we rinsed ours. Then he prayed Maghrib, and did not make fresh wudu’.’ In Ahmad 15990, Arna’ut: the chain is sahih.
footnotes.11: Sahih al-Bukhari 610 (from Anas (RA): on reaching a people at night he would not attack until morning; on hearing the adhan he would refrain, if not he would attack; narrated in the context of Khaybar itself); Sahih al-Bukhari 4197.
footnotes.12: Sahih al-Bukhari 4197 (from Anas (RA)); Sahih Muslim 1365. The sentence ‘evil is the morning of those who were warned’ uses the words of Surah al-Saffat 37:177, quoted in the hadith.
footnotes.13: Sirah-based: al-Rahiq al-Makhtum (Bengali), p. 618 (Ibn al-Qayyim, Zad al-Ma‘ad 2/139–140; Fath al-Bari 7/497; Ibn Hisham 2/337–338): Muslim martyrs at Khaybar, sixteen (four of Quraysh, one of Banu Ashja‘, one of Banu Aslam, one a local of Khaybar, the rest Ansari). In some narrations eighteen; ‘Allamah Sulayman Mansurpuri speaks of nineteen; in al-Rahiq’s words, by the sound view one was killed at Badr. Jews killed: ninety-three by unanimous agreement. Sirah-based; the chain has not been verified in this dars, so it has come as a scene, not as evidence.
footnotes.14: Sahih al-Bukhari 4243 (from ‘A’ishah (RA): ‘when Khaybar was conquered we said, now we will eat dates to our fill’); 4242 (the same statement, via ‘Ikrimah). In al-Albani, Sahih al-Targhib 3278, another narration of the same sense from ‘A’ishah (RA): ‘after the conquest of Qurayzah we got some dates and fat’. Both chains are sahih.
footnotes.15: Tawdih al-Qur’an, vol. 3, Surah al-Fath 48:20–21, p. 374 (matched word for word by reading the printed page); note 17: a hint toward conquests other than Khaybar; note 18: the obstruction the Jews of Khaybar and their allies could have created, which Allah has held back; note 19: ‘another victory’ means the conquest of Makkah and the Hunayn and other victories that followed it.

quiz.q: On the Day of Dhu Qarad, whom did the Prophet ﷺ call ‘our best horseman today’?
quiz.e: And the best infantryman was Salamah; Muslim 1807.

quiz.q: In which Hijri year did the Khaybar expedition take place?
o: The end of the sixth year
quiz.e: At the beginning of 7 AH, on returning from Hudaybiyah.

quiz.q: According to the note in Tawdih al-Qur’an, who received permission to go on the Khaybar expedition?
o: A special selected group of the Ansar
quiz.e: It is stated in the note on Surah al-Fath 48:15.

quiz.q: Who was driving the camels on the way to Khaybar, singing poetry?

o: The stone wall of the fortress collapsed
His own sword came back and struck him
quiz.e: The sword was short; it came back and struck his own knee.

quiz.q: In reply to ‘‘Amir’s deeds have been wasted’, what did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: His matter is in Allah’s hand
He will not get the rank of a martyr
quiz.e: He said, whoever said this has said wrongly; for him are two rewards.

quiz.q: What is learned from the Prophet’s ﷺ reply about ‘Amir’s death?
o: There is no reward for death by accident
Reciting poetry is forbidden in war
The decision that no one with a short sword should go to war
No hasty judgement about the outcome of others’ deeds
quiz.e: Outwardly an accident; with Allah, two rewards.

quiz.q: After someone’s death people are making bad remarks about their deeds; what does this dars teach?
o: Not passing judgement by outward appearance
Informing their family of the matter
quiz.e: About ‘Amir the Prophet ﷺ said, whoever said so has said wrongly.

quiz.q: Not found on the journey of hardship, first present on the journey of profit; in which incident is this picture found?
o: Those left behind wanting to go along
The accident of ‘Amir’s sword and people’s verdict
The Prophet’s ﷺ joy on seeing Ja‘far

quiz.q: On reaching a settlement at night, what did the Prophet ﷺ do before attacking?
o: Raid stealthily in the very darkness of night
Wait for the adhan until morning
Send an envoy with a letter
quiz.e: On hearing the adhan he would refrain; only if he did not hear it would he attack.

quiz.q: What did the people of Khaybar come out with in the morning?
quiz.e: They had come out for work in the fields.

quiz.q: Seeing the people of Khaybar, which sentence did the Prophet ﷺ say?
o: Allah alone is our only helper

quiz.q: What is the significance of waiting for the adhan even on a night of war?
o: No sword in a settlement of Allah’s name
Fighting at night is physically hard
A strategy of letting the enemy sleep
Giving the soldiers time to pray
quiz.e: Where the adhan is called, there is no attack.
